Thanks again for the call earlier — good discussion. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before we bring Aditya in for technical sizing: 

What I heard as your high-level requirements:
- Latency (p95) targets: US < 200 ms, EU < 250 ms, APAC < 400 ms for interactive chat paths.
- Throughput: steady-state ~150–250 req/s across peak windows, with spikes up to ~400 req/s for a few minutes.
- Concurrency: typical per-instance concurrency ~20–30 concurrent users/streams.
- Streaming: you need chunked token-by-token streaming (server push) for the UI for both chat and long-form generation.
- Regional routing / residency: EU customer traffic and any logs/analytics for EU users must remain in EU; APAC preference for Singapore region; US traffic in us-west/us-east.

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm the p95 targets above are accurate? Any different targets for non-interactive batches (e.g., embeddings or async batch jobs)?
2) Please share a representative payload (avg token lengths, prompt sizes) and an estimate of percent streaming vs non-streaming traffic.
3) I will loop in Aditya (solutions engineering) to validate feasibility and provide a rough sizing + deployment recommendation (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

- Data residency: must ensure EU user data (requests, logs, derived telemetry) stays physically in EU for at least 7 days before any transfer; we may request longer retention controls later. APAC: preferences are Singapore region for latency; not strictly prohibited from leaving APAC but prefer regional processing + storage where possible.
- Fallbacks: if regional capacity is constrained, we'd prefer regional fallback to a lower-cost EU/US variant with clear notice rather than routing traffic to an out-of-region private cluster.

Can Aditya confirm whether Redwood can meet the p95 targets with streaming for the given payloads, and what deployment model you'd recommend (hosted vs dedicated vs private) to meet residency + latency constraints? Also want a rough cost delta for dedicated vs hosted for our expected qps.

Thanks for the context and the payload numbers — helpful. High-level technical assessment and recommended next steps below. I'll keep this concise; happy to expand on any bullet in a sync.

Feasibility (interactive streaming p95 targets):
- US (us-west / us-east): achievable at p95 ~120–180 ms for streaming responses with a medium-sized causal model (quantized) when using dedicated pools + token streaming enabled.
- EU (eu-west): achievable at p95 ~170–240 ms in EU regions with dedicated capacity and regional KV/prefix caching. Expect ~20–30% higher latency vs US due to region network differences in our benchmarks.
- APAC (sg): streaming p95 ~300–420 ms depending on model variant; if you need consistently <300 ms in APAC we recommend a local APAC private deployment or dedicated reserve in SG region (adds infra/ops cost).

Throughput / concurrency sizing:
- For ~180 steady req/s with 420 req/s burst and concurrency ~25, rough starting point is a 3–4 GPU dedicated pool (A100 vs 80GB variants depending on model), plus autoscaling headroom for bursts. If you plan to use a larger model family or non-quantized weights, add ~30–50% capacity.

- Continuous batching and prefix caching will reduce per-token cost and improve tail latency; we recommend enabling KV cache for chat contexts and using our streaming-optimized kernel paths.

Streaming requirements:
- Redwood supports chunked token streaming (server-sent events / chunked HTTP). For 65% streaming traffic as you noted, network and client buffering are the main contributors to end-to-end latency — we can provide recommended client-side settings (chunk size, flush frequency) in the runbook.

Regional routing & data residency options:
- EU residency: two options — (1) Hosted with regional tenancy (we provision EU-only tenant + regional data storage + KMS in EU) for most customers; or (2) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with full physical control for strict regulatory needs. Hosted regional tenancy gives the best balance of speed and operational simplicity.
- Fallbacks: Redwood supports policy-based routing: prefer local region -> fallback to secondary region (configurable) with clear observability events. We can tag requests so logs/telemetry originating from EU stay in EU; when fallback occurs we can redact or limit telemetry export per your policy.

Cost and deployment recommendation:
- Recommendation: start with a Dedicated Reserved pool in US + EU, with a small APAC burst pool (or Hosted in APAC if lower cost) OR run a Private lightweight APAC node if consistent low-latency is critical.
- Cost delta (very rough): Dedicated Reserved typically ~1.8x–3x hosted per-token cost depending on commitment and autoscaling profile — but gives predictable latency/SLOs and simplifies meeting EU residency. We'll provide a tailored estimate once we know model family and commitment term.

Next steps / asks from Finova:
1) Share a small sample payload set (3–5 representative requests) and a short traffic timeline for a 24h window so we can run a bench.
2) Tell us which model family you prefer (open models vs Redwood-verified variants). If undecided, we'll run a short A/B on a compact and a medium variant.
3) Approve a short perf trial: we can run a 2–4 hour dedicated perf run (by appointment) to validate p95 and throughput.

I'll update the attached SLO_Matrix_v2.pdf with these notes and include an initial sizing sketch. Also attaching a simple network topology that shows regional flows and recommended fallbacks.
